candidates: Optimizer default parameter values should be stored as a class-level `defaults` dict that extends the parent class's defaults (e.g., `defaults = {**Optimizer.defaults, 'alpha': 70.0}`), keeping them close to the class implementation rather than in a separate centralized defaults module.

Library code must not call `print()` to stdout or stderr — those streams belong to the caller. Route optimizer diagnostic output through the instance's logfile attribute or the standard `logging` module.

Do not use `warnings.warn()` for common, recoverable algorithm events such as step-size scaling or a Hessian having negative eigenvalues; these are normal occurrences that the algorithm handles automatically and should instead be written to the optimizer's logfile.

When changing existing default parameter values in optimizer classes (e.g., `maxstep`), flag the change explicitly in the review — users' simulations depend silently on these defaults, and any modification will alter behavior without a visible API change.
New entries in `doc/releasenotes.rst` must be placed under the correct section heading (e.g., optimizer changes belong under 'Algorithms', not under 'I/O' or other unrelated sections).
